question: If AI agents can switch on the lights and lock the doors, what should still need a person's approval?
reflection: Tools that prove a photo is real can help people trust what they see again, and trust is the ground every community builds on.

sources.subject: Anthropic Claude adds Docs, Slides & Design: no app-switching

one_line: AI agents move into homes and office suites, while the US signals it is open to talking with China about shared AI risks.

top_stories.title: AI agents can now run smart homes
top_stories.what: Google opened an early-access connector that lets assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT control supported home devices and review their activity, for paying US users.
top_stories.why: Handing physical controls to an agent raises new questions on consent, household roles and error recovery that behavioural studies can answer.

top_stories.title: US says it is open to AI risk talks with China
top_stories.what: The US Treasury Secretary said shared AI risks could be discussed with China at talks this weekend, ahead of a planned leaders' summit.
top_stories.why: Any common ground between the two AI powers will shape the rules other countries, including Gulf states, adopt.

top_stories.title: Office tools built into the AI assistant
top_stories.what: Anthropic merged Claude's chat and background work modes and added document, slide and design tools in beta for paid plans.
top_stories.why: Research teams could draft reports and decks in one place, so it is worth testing how much review time this really saves.

saudi_lens.text: A new industry alliance wants data centres to cut power use when the grid is stretched; Saudi planners could ask for the same flexibility as the Kingdom's data-centre capacity grows in a hot climate.

idea.title: Who controls the smart home
idea.pitch: Interview families about which home tasks they would hand to an AI agent and which must stay with a person, and why.
idea.first_step: Write a list of ten home actions, from dimming lights to unlocking doors, and pilot it with five households.

idea_kids.title: Real or made-up photo detective kit
idea_kids.pitch: A classroom kit where children compare printed photos and look for clues about whether an image was changed.
idea_kids.first_step: Print ten pairs of everyday photos, one original and one lightly edited, and write a clue sheet.
